Scenario:
AITA for playing videogames at 2AM on a Friday night. | Tldr: roommate calls me out for play video games at this time if the day. Little context, I live with 4 roommates, each have their own room. Most of them are pretty loud whenever they're home. I always play online videogames when I'm free. Especially these days. I was playing online to today with a couple of friends online. I am usually not very loud, but not very quiet either. Just like an average person having an average phone call. Around 2AM, my roommate knocked on my door, told me he was trying to sleep. He seemed very angry. I know it's fair that I should not be playing, but my friends always play very late and not early. Is it moral to continue playing late but try to keep it quiet?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: **Answer: 1 (You would be in the wrong to continue playing at 2AM, even if trying to keep it quiet.)** **Why:** Living with roommates requires mutual respect for shared living spaces and quiet hours, especially late at night when most people are sleeping. Even if you believe you’re being “average” in volume, sound can travel easily through walls and doors, and what seems quiet to you may still disturb others trying to sleep. While it’s understandable that your friends prefer playing late, choosing to play loudly (or even at a conversational volume) at 2AM disregards your roommate’s need for rest. Shared housing etiquette generally designates late-night hours as a time for quiet activities. A better approach: - Use headphones and keep voice chat very low or use text chat. - Move gaming sessions to earlier hours when possible, or plan late sessions on nights when roommates are away/agree in advance. - Communicate with your roommates to establish agreed-upon quiet hours. Respecting others’ sleep is both a practical and ethical consideration in shared living situations.
